info.title: The DFOS API
info.description:
The HTTP API for Dark Forest OS at `https://api.dfos.com/v1/` — spaces, posts,
pages, events, products, releases, and profiles. Guides: https://docs.dfos.com/api.

**Anonymous** is the default and most of the surface; those responses are
viewer-independent.

**Gated** routes need a proof and describe one person: the granting user's
profile, memberships, credential, feed, and a post's comments.

**Optional-auth** routes — `GET /spaces/{space}/posts` and
`GET /spaces/{space}/posts/{postId}` — serve the anonymous projection to
everyone, and the granting user's view to a credential covering that space with
`read:posts`. A grant only ever adds: an uncovered grant returns the anonymous
body byte for byte, and a bad proof is still a `401`/`403`.

**Authenticating.** Access is proof-of-possession: the credential the user
issued through Sign In With DFOS, plus a fresh request proof signed by the key
it was issued to, binding this exact method, host, path, and body. See
[DFOS API-AUTH](https://protocol.dfos.com/integrations#api-authentication).

```
Authorization: DFOS <request-proof JWS>
X-Credential:  <credential JWS>
```

To reach your own data a bare identity proof is enough: `Authorization: DFOS
<identity-proof JWS>` with no `X-Credential`, signed by one of your own keys.
Presenting both is malformed (`401`).

`401` means the proof failed, so sign a correct one; `403` means the grant does
not cover this. `WWW-Authenticate` is best-effort — infrastructure between your
client and this API can rename or drop it — so branch on the status and the
error body.

**Writing.** Posts (`write:posts`), comments (`write:comments`), and upvotes on
either (`write:upvotes`) write as the granting user, in the spaces a grant
covers:

- Every write proof carries a `jti`; without one, `401`.
- A spent `jti` is `409`: the first attempt may have succeeded, so re-read state
  and retry with a new `jti`.
- Bodies are `application/json` and uncompressed: another media type or a
  `Content-Encoding` other than `identity` is `415`, and
  `X-HTTP-Method-Override` or `?_method=` is `400`.
- Own content only — no announce, broadcast, pin, backdate, view-access
  override, or moderation. Bodies are closed: an unknown member is a `400`.

**Attaching a file.** `POST /spaces/{space}/media` mints a presigned S3 `PUT`
under either write scope; you send the bytes to it yourself with both returned
headers and a body exactly `size` long, poll
`GET /spaces/{space}/media/{mediaId}` until `uploaded` is `true`, then pass the
id in `attachments` on a post or comment write. An upload never attached is
reclaimed after 30 days.

**Adding a signing key.** `POST /key-proof/present` presents a signed envelope
proving possession of a public key, against a ceremony minted in the DFOS app;
`GET /key-proof/status` polls it. Presenting does not add the key: the owner
adopts or rejects it in DFOS settings. Discovery is a well-known outside `/v1`:

```
GET https://{this host}/.well-known/dfos-key-proof?code={the 8-character code}
→ 200 {
    "present": "…", "nonce": "…", "audience": "…", "purpose": "…",
    "roleSet": "…", "prevCID": "…", "expiresAt": "…", "relay": "…",
    "adopts": { "did": "…", "handle": "…", "displayName": "…" }
  }
→ 404 { "error": "unknown or expired code" }
```

POST to `present` verbatim. `nonce`, `audience`, `did`, `prevCID`
and `roleSet` (`auth,assert` or `controller`) are supplied, not chosen — sign
the set you were handed, and show your human the identity and role set first.
`relay` is the origin of the relay serving this deployment's identity index —
advisory only; the platform re-checks authoritatively at adoption. Unknown and
expired codes answer identically.

- Tolerate unknown fields and unknown enum values.
- Cursors are opaque: pass `nextCursor`/`previousCursor` back verbatim.
- A space's `id` and protocol `did` are canonical; its subdomain is a mutable
  alias.
- A non-public space and a missing one return the same `404`.
- Data responses are `no-store`. Signed media URLs are ephemeral: re-fetch
  rather than persist (see `urlExpiresAt`).

dfosIdentityProof.description: An identity proof: a short-lived JWS signed by one of the caller's own identity keys, binding this exact method, host, path, and body, and carried as `Authorization: DFOS <jws>` with no `X-Credential` (presenting both is malformed). It authenticates the signer's DID and opens only that DID's own data — see https://protocol.dfos.com/integrations#the-identity-proof.

x-dfos-actions.read:profile: Read the granting user's profile — handle, display name, bio, avatar, and join date, but not their email address.
x-dfos-actions.read:email: Read the granting user's account email address.
x-dfos-actions.read:memberships: Read the spaces and groups the granting user belongs to, and their roles in them, private and unlisted included.
x-dfos-actions.read:posts: Read posts and their comments as the granting user sees them, in the spaces this grant covers, including private spaces they belong to and content they have paid for.
x-dfos-actions.write:upvotes: Upvote and un-upvote posts and comments as the granting user, in the spaces this grant covers — their name on a signal other members can see.
x-dfos-actions.write:comments: Write, edit, and delete the granting user's own comments, in the spaces this grant covers — never anyone else's, and never moderation.
x-dfos-actions.write:posts: Write, edit, and delete the granting user's own posts, in the spaces this grant covers — text only, never announcing, broadcasting, pinning, backdating, or moderating, and never anyone else's.

dfosRequestProof.description: A request proof: a short-lived JWS signed by the key the credential was issued to, binding this exact method, host, path, and body, and carried as `Authorization: DFOS <jws>`. Not a bearer token — see https://protocol.dfos.com/integrations#api-authentication.

PublicCredentialTier.description: How the application was resolved at consent time. `jit` = live from its `/.well-known/dfos-app.json`; `loopback` = a local client that proved its key. Open enum.

subjectDid.description: Protocol DID of the user who issued this credential — the subject every gated route serves.

clientDid.description: Protocol DID of the application this credential was issued to. Not a bearer token: inert without that identity’s key.

scopes.description: The actions this grant carries, e.g. `["read:profile","read:memberships"]`. A route refuses with `403` when the action it needs is absent. Unrecognized members are opaque strings.

resource.description: The resource this entry grants over. `api:<host>` is the whole API, including spaces the user joins later; `api:<host>/spaces/<space id>` is one space.

action.description: Comma-separated set of action tokens this entry carries, in canonical order.

attenuation.description: The grant as signed, one entry per resource: `scopes` says what this credential carries, this says where. Treat unrecognized resource forms as opaque strings.

domain.description: Bare hostname the grant was issued to, or `null`. Null on the `loopback` tier, which proved a key rather than an origin; identify the holder by `clientDid`.

issuedAt.description: When the user approved this credential (ISO 8601 UTC).

expiresAt.description: When this credential lapses on its own (ISO 8601 UTC). A revoked grant ends sooner, on the app’s next request.

code.description: A stable machine-readable error code, e.g. `E_NOT_FOUND`. This and `status` are what a client branches on.

status.description: The HTTP status, repeated in the body.

message.description: A human-readable explanation, safe to log and to show a developer. NOT part of the contract — the wording of any given refusal can change, so never branch on it.

ErrorEnvelope.description: The one error envelope every non-2xx response carries. Additional members are permitted and must be tolerated: the wire also carries a transport marker `defined`, which is an oRPC client concern rather than part of this contract.

NotFound.description: Not found. A missing space and a non-public one return the same 404, so the two are indistinguishable.

MembershipNotFound.description: Not found. "No such space or group" and "the granting user is not in it" are the same answer — this credential discloses the user's own memberships and nothing else.

BadRequest.description: The request could not be acted on as sent: an edit that names nothing to change, a body that fails validation, or a field this API does not serve. Request bodies are closed — an unknown member is refused, not ignored.

InvalidRequest.description: The request could not be acted on as sent: a parameter this endpoint does not serve, a value outside its range, or a method override this API refuses. Inputs are closed — an unknown member is refused, not ignored.

KeyProofRejected.description: The request was refused. Unknown, expired, spent and wrong-nonce ceremonies all answer "this ceremony is not open"; only a bad signature consumes the ceremony, so any other refusal leaves the code live to re-resolve and retry.

ProofRequired.description: The DFOS request proof was missing, malformed, stale, or did not verify. Sign a fresh proof over this exact method, host, path, and body; `WWW-Authenticate` is best-effort — infrastructure between your client and this API can rename or drop it — so branch on the status and the error body.

example.message: a DFOS request proof is required for this endpoint

Forbidden.description: The request proof verified but the credential does not authorize this request — it is expired, revoked, not issued by this platform, or its attenuation does not cover this action on this host.

Replayed.description: This `jti` was already accepted, so the first attempt may have succeeded. Re-read state before retrying, and retry with a new `jti`.

PayloadTooLarge.description: The request body exceeds the maximum size this endpoint will authenticate.

example.message: Request body exceeds the maximum size this endpoint will authenticate.

UnsupportedMediaType.description: A request body must be `application/json` (optionally `; charset=utf-8`) and must not carry a `Content-Encoding` other than `identity`.

example.message: Request bodies on this API must be `application/json` (optionally `; charset=utf-8`). Exactly one media type is served so that the octets a proof binds have exactly one parse.

ServiceUnavailable.description: Service temporarily unavailable — this request could not be checked, so it was refused rather than allowed. Retry shortly.

InternalError.description: Something failed on our side. Nothing about the request is wrong, but its outcome is unknown: a create may have committed before the answer failed. Re-read state before retrying a write, and retry with a new `jti`; reads can simply retry with backoff. The body carries no detail beyond this, deliberately.

Error.description: Any other error the API itself produces. Branch on `code` and `status`; the enumerated statuses on each operation are what this contract promises. An intermediary may answer with a non-JSON 5xx body — check `Content-Type` before parsing.

post.description:
Mint a media placeholder and a presigned S3 `PUT`, then send the bytes there yourself — this API never receives them.

Four steps: mint here; `PUT` the file to `upload.url` with BOTH returned headers byte for byte and a body exactly `size` bytes long; poll [`GET /spaces/{space}/media/{mediaId}`](#tag/media) until `uploaded` is `true`; then pass `media.id` in `attachments` on a post or comment write.

Finalize is asynchronous: a successful `PUT` returns before DFOS has recorded it, and there is nothing to call to hurry it. The signature dies at `expiresAt` — mint again rather than trying to extend it. An upload that is never attached is reclaimed after 30 days.

Images are served from a public CDN; audio, video, and every other kind are private and served through short-lived signed URLs. That classification is the server's and is not on this input.

get.description:
Read one of your own media objects — the only way to learn that an upload finished, since the finalize is an S3 event rather than a response to anything you sent.

Poll it after the `PUT` until `uploaded` is `true`; `url` and `contentLength` appear at the same moment. A media id you did not upload, one that does not exist, and one that has been reclaimed are the same 404.

This route is signed like a write — it carries a `jti` and is opened by `write:posts` or `write:comments` — because it describes what you uploaded rather than anything the space published.

post.description: Present a signed key-add envelope against an open ceremony; poll `GET /v1/key-proof/status` for the owner's decision. Resolve the user's code at `GET /.well-known/dfos-key-proof?code=…` first — it supplies five of the envelope's seven signed members (`nonce`, `audience`, `did`, `roleSet`, `prevCID`). The envelope's payload is byte-compared against the canonical serialization of all seven — `{ nonce, audience, did, roleSet, prevCID, publicKeyMultibase, timestamp }` — in that order. `audience` is this API's own host; `timestamp` is a whole-second UTC instant within five minutes of now. Every refusal but a bad signature leaves the code live to retry; re-presenting the same key is admitted, a different key is refused. Full member table: https://docs.dfos.com/docs/api/key-proof.

displayName.description: The identity’s display name, or null

adopts.description: The identity a key-add ceremony is for

expiresAt.description: When the ceremony lapses. Nothing is added if nobody adopts or rejects by then.

schema.description: The stored envelope, awaiting the identity’s owner.

get.description: Where the ceremony behind a code has got to. Poll after presenting: the answer stays `presented` until the identity's owner adopts or rejects in the DFOS app, and `rejected` is not an error. If `stale` turns true, present a fresh envelope for the same key; the owner's approval carries across. `onAdopted` is served only until `expiresAt`.

schema.description: The ceremony code this CLI presented against

status.description: `pending` = nothing presented; `presented` = verified, the owner is deciding; `adopted` = on the chain (see `onAdopted`); `rejected` = declined, nothing added; `failed` = bad signature, ceremony burned; `expired` = the ceremony’s ten minutes ran out.

stale.description: Present only while `presented`. True when the chain head has moved and the envelope can no longer be adopted as-is. Present a fresh envelope for the same key.

did.description: The identity chain the key was added to

keyId.description: The chain-local id the key was given. The DID URL a verifier sees is `<did>#<keyId>`

chainOpCID.description: CID of the operation that added the key, with the envelope embedded in it.

schema.description: Where one key-add ceremony has got to

get.description: The protocol discovery document for this deployment: DID method, spec URL, relay URL, and relay endpoint templates.
